title: Imee, Robin to Marcos admin: Cease ICC cooperation, return ex-Pres Duterte to PH
summary: Senators Imee Marcos and Robin Padilla have filed a resolution urging the executive branch to immediately cease all cooperation with the International Criminal Court and exhaust all legal and…

blocks.text: Senators Imee Marcos and Robin Padilla have filed a resolution urging the executive branch to immediately cease all cooperation with the International Criminal Court and exhaust all legal and diplomatic means for the release and repatriation of former President Rodrigo Duterte.

In Senate Resolution 797 filed on November 25, Marcos and Padilla also urged the executive branch to discontinue efforts to serve the arrest warrant issued by the ICC against Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa.

They said the Philippines withdrew from the Rome Statute in 2019, terminating its status as a state party. However, despite pronouncements by authorities that the ICC has no jurisdiction in the country, Duterte was arrested and brought to The Hague, Netherlands, where he was turned over to the custody of the international court.
They added that authorities are also undertaking measures to locate, arrest, and turn over Dela Rosa to the ICC.

The senators also cited the joint Heads of State Declaration toward Peace issued by US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping "expressly recognizing that the principles of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials are of paramount importance and declaring that the ICC and similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction."

"In the exercise of its independent foreign policy, the Philippines must carefully consider significant developments in international relations, particularly when the positions articulated by major international partners bear directly upon matters affecting Philippine sovereignty, national interest, and the rights of Filipino citizens," Marcos and Padilla said.

They further said that the country's continued cooperation with the ICC, particularly in relation to the arrest of Duterte and the enforcement of an arrest warrant against Dela Rosa, must be reassessed.

"The pursuit of justice and accountability must remain consistent with the Constitution, the protection of fundamental rights, and the sovereign right of the Philippines to administer justice through its own institutions, without foreclosing accountability for crimes punishable under Philippine law," they said.
GMA News Online reached out to Malacañang for comment and will publish it once available. —AOL, GMA News
